Madam President, Madam Executive Director, dear members of the Board, dear colleagues, it is our pleasure to present the revised report of the Joint Working Group established to consider the recommendations contained in the Joint Inspection Unit review of the governance and oversight of the Executive Boards of UNDP, UNFPA, UNOPS, UNICEF and UN Women of 2023. I know it's a long title. Next slide. For those of you who are not so familiar with the whole process, just a very brief recap on where we stand and what happened so far. In 2023, the GIU review identified 10 formal and 21 informal recommendations in six thematic areas. And at the annual session 2024, the executive boards established the joint working group and tasked it with reviewing all 31 recommendations and developing actionable implementation pathways. The working group's terms of reference were formally adopted at the first regular session in 2025. And this year, at the first regular session and the annual session, the Joint Working Group presented its approach and interim report with proposals for all recommendations. We also held an informal meeting and Member States gave us written feedback on our proposals. Here at the second regular session today, we are presenting you with a revised report that includes an updated implementation plan in Annex 1. Just two points on the leading principles. It is always very important to emphasize that the working group advises and the Executive Board decides. So we just make proposals and of course you Member States decide. The joint working group has been guided by the overarching principle of strengthening and optimizing existing mechanisms of the Executive Boards wherever possible before proposing the creation of new structures. This approach is deliberately aligned with the objectives of the UN80 initiative, which calls for lean, efficient and effective governance across the UN system. Next slide, please. As can be seen here, the group has not accepted all of the GIU recommendations. Recommendations proposed for non-acceptance generally relate to matters considered adequately addressed. through existing arrangements where the working group judges that intervention would add procedural complexity without commensurate benefits. Because many of the recommendations are interrelated and built on one another, the working group has undertaken an indicative clustering of interrelated recommendations into five broad work packages that we would like to briefly introduce. I'll start with the first two. Among the key proposals of the working group is the development of a comprehensive harmonized informal guiding document, a delegates handbook, to be jointly drafted by the secretariats of all five organizations. The handbook would consolidate the roles, responsibilities, and procedures of executive board members, covering governance, oversight, risk management, and secretarial arrangements. It would address the substance of several related recommendations, can be updated as needed, and avoids duplication. The draft would be submitted to the Executive Boards for consideration, allowing for structured discussion and further refinement as needed. Second, we propose a dedicated review of the working methods of the Executive Boards of the participating organizations. followed by periodic assessments at agreed intervals. This review would address the harmonization of work plans, the relationship between informal and formal meetings, the quality and clarity of Board decisions, and the inclusiveness of Member State participation. It would also provide the appropriate context for further consideration of the possible advisory subcommittee mentioned above. And Another part of this working package is our proposal to explore the possible establishment of such a standing advisory committee covering audit, risk, budget and finance, composed of a limited number of member state experts with equitable geographical representation. And this proposal requires further consideration regarding its mandate, reporting arrangements and interaction with the boards, ensuring complementarity with existing oversight bodies and preserving the primacy of the boards in decision making. For the other working packages, I'll hand over to my co-colleague, Nicolai. Thank you, Nicolai.

Thank you, Annette, and good morning, colleagues. So the next work package is on the secretariats, and it concerns the development of harmonized terms of reference across the different executive board secretariats. And the aim is to clarify common elements such as roles, responsibilities, reporting lines, and the principle of impartiality. Next is oversight and advisory committees, and this package concerns the relationship between the existing audit and oversight committees and the executive boards. And these committees already report annually to the executive boards and engage with board members through informal consultation. And our proposal is therefore to update the relevant terms of reference and charters to provide for a direct reporting line to the executive boards in addition to the existing relationship with the executive heads, as well as to ensure unrestricted access to the boards. Finally, under AOB, several additional recommendations are brought together, including the possible performance review of executive heads, orientation and onboarding, uh, of board members, and the role of the executive boards in risk management, and let me briefly explain this, these three elements. So on performance review, group recognizes that the introduction of a formalized review mechanism would require further careful consideration, particularly with regard to the appropriate criteria, methodology, and information sources in order to ensure an objective and balanced assessment. And possible options for further exploration could include a limited number of outcome-oriented objectives linked to the executive heads approved job description and the organization's strategic frameworks. On training and orientation, a group supports greater harmonization and common standards for the onboarding of executive board members. However, rather than establishing a single common training program across all agencies, the proposal is for the respective secretariats to jointly develop harmonized minimum standards for orientation and onboarding. On risk management, the group found that the existing risk management policies of agencies already generally reflect the oversight role of the boards and the proposal is for the agencies to undertake a joint review and comparison of the existing risk management frameworks, including reporting modalities to the boards, to provide for greater alignment and coherence. And next slide, please. On the next step, the joint working group will continue its work with a view to further developing possible implementation modalities and facilitating the implementation of recommendations where and as decided by the boards. Six. recalls General Assembly resolution 48/162 and 50/227, and reaffirms the Executive Board's responsibility within its mandate to consider and recommend any proposed structural changes to United Nations entities under its governance, while following the existing legal framework as well as established procedural step and in this regard to issue a recommendation on the potential merger or alternative options through a decision to be transmitted to the Economic and Social Council and through the Council to the General Assembly as necessary before a decision on a potential is scheduled for consideration by the General Assembly. 7. Recalls General Assembly resolutions 79/318 and 80/155, and reaffirms the central role of Member States in the reform process, which should be inclusive, evidence-based and transparent, and, in this regard, calls on UN Women to actively engage with members and observers of the Executive Board. Eight, strongly emphasizes that any structural reform must fully safeguard the integrity of the triple mandate of UN Women and demonstrably strengthen country level delivery. Nine, recalls decision 2026/15, taking note of the legal elements on the potential merger of UN Women and UNFPA provided by the legal office of UN Women. which states, inter alia, that there is no specific legal mechanism available to guarantee the continuity of existing mandates, which therefore may be adjusted or redefined at the time of a merger or thereafter. 10. Further recalls Decision 2026/15, taking note of the internal UNFPA legal advice, which indicates that there are risks for the integrity of the mandates of the two entities in case of a merger. 11, decides that the Executive Board, while remaining committed to engaging constructively with the UN80 Initiative, is not in a position to make a recommendation of support on a potential merger between UNFPA and UN Women at this time. and at least not before the next formal meeting of the Executive Board, and alleging inter alia that the protection of mandates cannot be guaranteed, and affirming the importance of ensuring coherence and alignment among ongoing reforms, as well as the continuity to country-level delivery. 12. encourages UN Women to explore implementation of alternative options within its authority, including enhanced governance, coordination, and country-level delivery, to enhance system-wide coherence and efficiency, without preempting a possible recommendation by the Executive Board on a potential merger, and request that the Executive Board be kept informed. 13, request the Bureau, in collaboration with the Bureau of UNDP, UNFPA, UNEP, to explore ways to improve further engagement of the Executive Boards on the UN80 Initiative as appropriate to contribute to any possible recommendation on the matter. So we, of course, will miss the calls and communications, but please consider your friends and will be all the time very happy to hear from you good news from somewhere in the sea or wherever you would like to have your future. So all the best to you and thank you very much indeed on behalf of the Executive Board, us of the Bureau. We have really appreciated the cooperation with you. So with that, I would like to give you The floor. Belgium would like to take the floor. Belgium, Permanent Representative, dear Sophie, the floor is yours.

Thank you very much, Madam President. Dear ED, thank you for creating this opportunity as well to thank Jean-Luc properly. Yesterday, we had three minutes for the statement. Dear Jean-Luc, 15 years as Secretary of the Board is really quite a commitment. And we all see the meetings, the decisions, the discussions, the outcomes. But few of us realize how many countless hours of preparation, coordination, and availability that this takes. And you not only make it possible, you also make it look effortless. Anyway, Jean-Luc, I wish you every happiness for this next chapter, and you have my gratitude. I thank you.
Thank you very much, Madam Permanent Representative of Belgium, for this very emotional address to Jean-Luc. Jean-Luc, can we avoid this or not?
I can do it.
You can do it. Okay. Now I give you the floor, Mr. Secretary, dear Jean-Luc, you have the floor.

Thank you very much, Madam President. I promised myself I wouldn't cry, but... But thank you very much.
